content: The World Health Organization (WHO) published a guideline in 2017 focusing on school health services. In 2021, WHO released a school handbook on life skills education, specifically addressing approaches for schools to tackle noncommunicable diseases. Additionally, WHO and UNAIDS developed global standards for quality health-care services for adolescents, providing a comprehensive guide to implementing a standards-driven approach to enhance the quality of adolescent health care. This guidance is divided into three volumes: 1. Volume 1 outlines the standards and criteria for adolescent health-care services. 2. Volume 2 serves as an implementation guide for these standards. 3. WHO has also emphasized the importance of making every school a health-promoting school, offering implementation guidance to achieve this goal. Experiences from the Western Pacific Region have been documented in a report by the WHO Regional Office for the Western Pacific in 2017. Similarly, a consultation on health-promoting schools in the Eastern Mediterranean Region was conducted by the WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean in 2005. In terms of cost-effective strategies to improve global learning, recent evidence highlights smart buys for enhancing education outcomes in lowand middle-income countries. WHO has also developed various assessment tools, including: A tool for conducting gap analysis against global standards for health-promoting schools. School health profiles. A physical education curriculum analysis tool. The Health Education Curriculum Analysis Tool (HECAT). The School Health Index, which is a self-assessment and planning guide available as an e-learning module. A rapid assessment and action planning process. These resources collectively aim to support schools in improving health education, physical education, and overall health promotion efforts.
